dimensions.label: Privacy and confidentiality

S1.criterion: Affirmative bounded evidence establishes zero unauthorised access, exposure, processing or disclosure of personal or confidential information where confidentiality was directly tested; silence about misuse does not negate a proven disclosure.

S2.criterion: Confirmed limited low-sensitivity disclosure or unauthorised processing, indicatively involving 1–99 unique people and promptly contained without substantiated consequential misuse; OR confirmed unauthorised access to, acquisition of, or processing of real non-public personal or confidential information even when the sensitivity, number of affected people, exposure duration, recovery and subsequent misuse are unknown. The confirmed protected-information access is an S2 minimum evidenced harm, not proof that the full consequence is minor; record unresolved higher severity separately. Mere public information retrieval, vulnerability discovery, speculative access or unverified allegation does not satisfy this minimum.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but containable exposure, unauthorised access or misuse of protected, credential or confidential information, illustratively involving 100–9,999 people, or fewer people where sensitivity or access consequence is material. Assess actual disclosure, exposure hours and containment.

S4.criterion: Large-scale confirmed disclosure, illustratively 10,000 or more uniquely affected people, or highly sensitive information exposure, persistent loss of confidentiality or substantial evidenced misuse. A small, exceptionally sensitive disclosure can independently qualify; record accessibility, uncontrolled copies and actual affected population.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic and effectively irreversible confidentiality loss producing grave safety, liberty or societal consequences, including for one critically vulnerable person. Count exposed records and persons, but numerical volume alone never qualifies as S5.

dimensions.adaptation_note: Distinguish unauthorised access or disclosure from evidenced downstream misuse. Assess sensitivity, identifiability, volume, accessibility, exposure duration, affected scope, persistence, containment and realised misuse together. Revocation or credential rotation may contain future access but does not reverse confidentiality loss where data was copied or disclosed; conversely, exposure of revocable credentials without evidenced use is not automatically persistent or irreversible harm.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Financial and economic

S1.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss below USD 10,000, provided the evidence does not establish material livelihood or organisational-viability impairment.

S2.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss of at least USD 10,000 and below USD 1,000,000, or independently evidenced low and readily remediable economic disruption where no defensible USD conversion is available.

S3.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss of at least USD 1,000,000 and below USD 100,000,000, or independently evidenced material but bounded livelihood or organisational loss where no defensible USD conversion is available.

S4.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss of at least USD 100,000,000 and below USD 100,000,000,000, or independently evidenced substantial solvency, organisational-viability or widespread economic impact where no defensible USD conversion is available.

S5.criterion: Aggregate direct realised loss of at least USD 100,000,000,000, catastrophic insolvency or systemic economic loss.

dimensions.adaptation_note: The five quantitative anchors are informed by the MIT FutureTech 2026 Delphi severity work. VIGIL extends S4 through amounts below USD 100 billion to close the otherwise unclassified USD 10 billion to below USD 100 billion interval. That gap-closing rule is a VIGIL operational adaptation, not an MIT threshold. Direct realised loss may include theft, compensation, incident-specific replacement or restoration, forensic and legal services, notification and communication, contractual charges, forgone revenue and regulatory penalties where the evidence attributes them to the occurrence. Ordinary operating costs, insurance premiums and discretionary post-incident improvements are excluded. Do not infer an amount from effort, notoriety or asset importance.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Property and asset damage

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes zero destruction, corruption, loss or impairment of physical or digital assets where asset integrity was directly at issue.

S2.criterion: Minor, localised, fully reversible damage to one or more non-critical physical or digital assets, with routine recovery indicatively within 7 days; OR confirmed unauthorised alteration, deletion or corruption of persisted real third-party data or operational records, causing loss of expected data-integrity state, even where the scope, reversibility and recovery burden are unknown. This second pathway establishes an S2 minimum, not a finding that any larger harm was absent. Record affected assets and actual changes where available; do not equate mere server access, unaltered data reads, synthetic test artefacts or unverified allegations with demonstrated integrity loss.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded asset destruction, corruption or unauthorised modification requiring material reconstruction or recovery, often over approximately 7–30 days. Quantify affected assets, days of recovery and directly evidenced restoration value.

S4.criterion: Substantial destruction or loss of important or critical assets requiring major recovery, often over 30 days, while technically and operationally viable reconstruction remains. One critical asset may suffice; assess actual loss of trusted state.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic or effectively irreversible destruction of a critical physical or digital asset, including loss of trustworthy operational state requiring clean-room reconstruction where that loss is itself catastrophic. One such asset suffices; precautionary reimaging alone does not qualify.

dimensions.adaptation_note: Asset damage is assessed independently from realised financial loss. Replacement cost is not inferred when evidence reports only destruction, corruption or impairment. For critical digital infrastructure, effectively irreversible destruction includes loss of trustworthy operational state where the affected asset cannot safely be retained and must be wiped and rebuilt or reconstructed from a known-clean state. Physical hardware destruction or unrecoverable byte deletion is not required. Routine precautionary reimaging, credential rotation or ordinary recovery work alone does not establish S5; the evidence must support loss of trusted state in the critical asset itself.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Service, operational and infrastructure

S1.criterion: No user-visible impairment, or a positively evidenced non-critical interruption below 15 minutes contained within recovery objectives.

S2.criterion: Limited non-critical degradation below two hours; critical-service interruption below 30 minutes; a localised workflow failure resolved by routine recovery; OR confirmed unauthorised cancellation or alteration of a real third party's valid booking, waitlist position, transaction or service entitlement that materially changes that party's operational state, regardless of whether later restoration or duration is reported. The final alternative establishes only an S2 minimum and does not infer that the disruption was short-lived, fully reversible or the complete consequence. Mere exploitation of a booking endpoint without an affected transaction or service state does not qualify.

S3.criterion: Material disruption of an important service or workflow; critical or important function unavailable more than two hours; complete relevant cloud-service unavailability over 30 minutes; or limited availability affecting more than 5% or 1 million EU users (whichever is smaller) for more than one hour, with bounded recovery. Count users actually disrupted, not merely registered.

S4.criterion: Essential or critical operation disrupted for more than 24 hours; substantial multi-organisation or multi-jurisdiction operational impact; exceeded evidenced maximum tolerable downtime; or major external recovery intervention. A production compromise alone, without evidenced operational impact, is insufficient.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic or prolonged essential-service loss or operational collapse with independently evidenced grave consequences. Record downtime, actual user interruptions and service criticality; no generic minimum of one million users applies.

dimensions.adaptation_note: The time and scope anchors adapt CISA, NIST, NIS2 and DORA concepts. Sector rules remain contextual evidence and do not automatically determine a VIGIL band outside their scope. Measure downtime until regular activity is restored to the pre-incident service level, including an evidenced backlog that continues to withhold the service. Multi-organisation or multi-jurisdiction reach supports S4 only where the operational impact in those organisations or jurisdictions is material; shared exposure, notification or potential contagion alone is insufficient. Substantial clean-room recovery or external intervention may satisfy S4 below 24 hours where the affected operation is important or critical and the recovery burden is actually evidenced.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

dimensions.label: Reputation and dignity

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence of zero consequential false attribution, humiliation, impersonation or reputational/dignitary injury after checking the relevant publication or reliance chain. Absence of a public complaint alone is insufficient.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: 0 evidenced adverse reputational outcomes after a source-bounded check of the actual reliance and response chain; confirmation of no consequential attribution, correction burden or dignity injury (not silence).
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Affirmatively negligible/no reputational consequence; if the source is silent about reactions, use unreported or insufficient evidence rather than S1.

S2.criterion: Minor, localised embarrassment, offence or attribution error, including at least one documented attributable correction, apology or bounded dignitary affront, ordinarily corrected within 7 days, with no substantiated material loss of opportunity or standing.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: At least one source-confirmed public/professional correction, apology or attributable local reputational affront; illustrative effective correction within 7 days; zero independently evidenced material opportunity/role loss.
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Localized, minor and readily reversible embarrassment/attribution injury from relied-on defective content. Court filing or publication alone does not escalate.

S3.criterion: Meaningful, bounded humiliation, impersonation, false attribution or reputation damage with substantial prospects of correction, including at least one independently verified materially adverse third-party reliance reaction or lost bounded opportunity, or adverse standing indicatively lasting 8–30 days.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: At least one documented materially adverse external reliance reaction (e.g. professional credibility finding or lost bounded opportunity), or evidenced adverse standing lasting approximately 8–30 days; correction substantially feasible.
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Meaningful but bounded reputational deterioration. A formal correction without adverse standing beyond embarrassment stays S2.

S4.criterion: Severe, extensive or persistent dignitary/reputational harm with substantial consequences, including at least one verified major loss of livelihood, role or professional standing attributable to the occurrence, or adverse standing lasting indicatively 31–365 days with serious effects. Large audience alone is insufficient.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: At least one verified substantial livelihood/role/reputational setback or serious professional restriction materially grounded in a reliance event; or adverse standing evidenced approximately 31–365 days with substantial ongoing functional consequences.
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Substantial or widespread and persistent loss of standing; one person or organisation suffices. Large publication count alone does not.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic and effectively irreversible reputational or dignitary harm accompanied by grave safety, liberty or societal consequences, such as permanently non-restorable exclusion. One evidenced victim suffices; no minimum audience or 365-day waiting period applies.

epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.numeric: At least one evidenced catastrophic and effectively irreversible reputational/dignitary consequence with grave safety, liberty or societal effects; documented ongoing/prospective permanent exclusion or similarly non-restorable harm (no minimum audience and no need to wait 365 days to recognise irreversibility).
epistemic_downstream_reliance_threshold.outcome: Requires catastrophe plus the distinct grave consequence in the existing S5 criterion; no inference from scandal, virality or a speculative future career collapse.

dimensions.adaptation_note: Distinguish public exposure from reputational or dignitary injury. Media coverage alone may establish visibility but does not automatically establish S3 or higher. Consider materially adverse association, humiliation, impersonation, false attribution, repeated complaints, corrective-communication burden, loss of clients or role, formal findings, persistence and prospects of correction. Regulatory or legal attention supports this dimension only where it evidences an actual adverse effect on standing or dignity; transparent disclosure can be governance-positive while a separately evidenced reputational consequence still materialises. Where the preceding cause is an epistemic failure, distinguish the defective claim, actual downstream professional/institutional reliance, specific reputation-bearing target and independently observed adverse standing. Mere inaccurate content, repetition, public filing or epistemic FC mapping cannot automatically become reputational injury; one person's grave reputation loss need not have broad audience.
dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.

epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm.status: Operational domain recognition guidance; not a taxonomy class and not an automatic FC-to-HIM mapping
epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm.scope: A specific Incident with false, fabricated, distorted or low-assurance AI-mediated content can result in independently evidenced reputational injury when a relevant person or institution actually relies on it in a credibility-bearing setting. Harm may affect the subject falsely characterised OR the person/organisation that relied on and redistributed the claim.
epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm.mapping_rule: Epistemic classification describes the failure mechanism; reputational severity is a separate consequence determination. A class mapping, generated false citation, a false claim, public visibility or a hypothetical reliance chain does not by itself establish reputation-and-dignity harm.

downstream_chain.required_evidence: Source and artefact establish the material wrong statement, fabricated or misattributed citation, contaminated source, falsely certified research, or other concrete epistemic defect.

Identify the actual relying actor or process and consequential action: submitted official material, professional filing, institutional assertion, public attribution, consequential decision or demonstrably relied-on communication. Source references, recipient/action/date and version are needed. For direct demeaning speech or impersonation, reliance is not essential: score the independently evidenced dignitary injury directly.

Identify whose standing/dignity was adversely affected: wrongly accused subject, professional who presented the defective output, institution that adopted it, or another directly attributable party. Mere criticism of a model provider or publication of a correction does not automatically satisfy this.

Affirmative evidence of embarrassment, public retraction with negative reception, credibility challenge, loss of trust, correction obligation, formal finding, lost role/contract, documented professional sanction or ongoing inability to restore standing. Measure separately from financial loss, service delay and technical error.

counting_rules: One fabricated assertion copied 50 times is not 50 independent injuries. Count unique actual reliance actions/recipients and consequences with provenance, avoiding duplicate publication chains.
Audience reach and media coverage can explain persistence, but raw impressions or platform audience do not establish loss of standing.
Professional embarrassment after a verified public corrective filing may support S2, not automatically S3 because a court is involved.
One individual's confirmed loss of career or irremediable dignitary injury can satisfy S4/S5 as warranted even when no audience count or population threshold is reached.

A false output never externally used may be an epistemic/taxonomy failure with reputational harm unreported, not a fabricated minimal severity. A privately delivered demeaning output may separately support dignity injury without third-party reliance.
Do not score the same financial loss, courtroom delay or rights deprivation again as reputational harm absent distinct evidenced injury to standing or dignity.
Where actual reliance is not demonstrated, do not infer materialised reputational harm from plausible opportunities for reliance.
epistemic_reliance_to_reputational_harm.specific_vs_aggregate_harm: Use this observed-consequence chain ONLY for a particular actual person, group, organisation or other bounded reputation-bearing subject. Never apply generic deployed-model population bands to that specific Incident. For a generic deployed benchmark with no evidenced injured subject, candidate Aggregate Harm requires a separate proven pathway and the currently approved five-domain Aggregate Harm pilot does not yet include reputation-dignity.

calibration_cases.observation: Phantom Claude legal quotations filed in federal court; counsel made public correction and apology
calibration_cases.reason: Bounded public professional embarrassment with correction, not necessarily formal sanction or sustained credibility loss.

calibration_cases.observation: Fictitious legal authorities in Victorian proceedings; counsel apologised and court was delayed
calibration_cases.reason: Corrective apology supports minor professional embarrassment; case delay is operational, not automatic extra reputational impact.

calibration_cases.observation: Fabricated references propagated into parliamentary submissions and some committee reporting
calibration_cases.reason: Reliance/propagation is evidenced, but independent reputational loss to a particular submitter, committee, researcher or organisation has not been established.

calibration_cases.observation: Gemini privately delivered directly demeaning statements to a user
calibration_cases.reason: Direct dignitary offence can materialise without a third party relying on the statement.

dimensions.label: Societal and democratic

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes zero consequential collective, civic, democratic-process or public-information harm where such impact was directly at issue.
S1.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1–9,999 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support minimal bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S2.criterion: Minor, localised civic or collective information impact confined to a bounded community or process, promptly corrected. Record the verified audience, actual affected share and correction time.
S2.aggregate_harm_threshold: 10,000–999,999 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support minor aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded disruption of a community, civic process, public institution or information environment. Assess independently evidenced persons or community share affected, institutional effects and restoration days; one important local process may suffice.
S3.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000,000–9,999,999 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support meaningful but bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S4.criterion: Substantial and persistent cross-community, multi-jurisdiction or institutional/democratic-process impact, including disruptions across decision cycles. Quantify community/electorate share, institutions and duration; raw media impressions do not establish harm.
S4.aggregate_harm_threshold: 10,000,000–99,999,999 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support substantial or widespread aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic and enduring systemic civic or democratic destabilisation, including gravely impaired essential institutional function. Quantify affected institutions, relevant population share and decision cycles; a fixed global headcount is not necessary where the institutional consequences are catastrophic.
S5.aggregate_harm_threshold: at least 100,000,000 relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence. Independently, the case evidence must support grave or catastrophic systemic aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

dimensions.quantification_note: Numerical durations, event counts and population measures are evidence-tested domain anchors within each S1–S5 criterion, not independent automatic scores. Judge seriousness, causal contribution and reversibility; a grave individual outcome needs no large exposed population.
dimensions.selective_deployment_scale_note: Relevant where the failure can affect information environments, social coordination or civic choices at community/population scale; measure share of relevant audience and distribution, not platform headline size.

aggregate_harm_assessment.population_or_decision_metric: relevant audience on a confirmed civic distribution or decision pathway
aggregate_harm_assessment.mechanism_condition: A demonstrable process or distribution mechanism with a credible collective information, participation or institution-level consequence.
aggregate_harm_assessment.notes: Source-backed relevant eligible users/decisions in a deployed tested path, not injured persons or total platform accounts. Use only for generic model-level evaluation with no specific actual harmed person or group. Numeric brackets are VIGIL 1.1.0 operational gates, reviewed through future calibration.
aggregate_harm_assessment.routing: Use only when assessment_pathway_selection selects generic deployed-model evaluation with no particular harmed individual/group; not a modifier of ordinary specific-Incident severity.

dimensions.label: Environmental and animal welfare

S1.criterion: For every ecological or animal-welfare pathway directly at issue, positive bounded evidence establishes no material biophysical degradation, injury, suffering or impairment. Source silence is not S1.
S1.ecological_criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes zero material biophysical degradation where environmental consequence was directly assessed.
S1.animal_welfare_criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes no material injury, suffering or impairment where animal welfare was directly at issue.

S2.criterion: Ecological pathway: Minor, localised, readily reversible ecological damage, with recovery illustratively within 30 days. Record verified habitat area, pollutant loads and treatment rather than human audience numbers. Animal-welfare alternative: Minor, temporary pain, distress or injury, with straightforward recovery and no lasting impairment.
S2.ecological_criterion: Minor, localised, readily reversible ecological damage, with recovery illustratively within 30 days. Record verified habitat area, pollutant loads and treatment rather than human audience numbers.
S2.animal_welfare_criterion: Minor, temporary pain, distress or injury, with straightforward recovery and no lasting impairment.

S3.criterion: Ecological pathway: Meaningful but bounded ecological damage requiring active remediation, with restoration indicatively taking 30–365 days. Record hectares affected, pollutant concentrations, exceedances and affected ecosystem functions. Animal-welfare alternative: Serious but recoverable injury, illness or suffering requiring substantial treatment or rehabilitation.
S3.ecological_criterion: Meaningful but bounded ecological damage requiring active remediation, with restoration indicatively taking 30–365 days. Record hectares affected, pollutant concentrations, exceedances and affected ecosystem functions.
S3.animal_welfare_criterion: Serious but recoverable injury, illness or suffering requiring substantial treatment or rehabilitation.

S4.criterion: Ecological pathway: Substantial, persistent or cross-jurisdiction ecological degradation, often requiring more than 365 days of remediation or producing serious multi-region ecosystem effects. Area alone does not determine severity; assess critical functions and reversibility. Animal-welfare alternative: Death, permanent major impairment, or severe prolonged suffering affecting an individual animal or a bounded group.
S4.ecological_criterion: Substantial, persistent or cross-jurisdiction ecological degradation, often requiring more than 365 days of remediation or producing serious multi-region ecosystem effects. Area alone does not determine severity; assess critical functions and reversibility.
S4.animal_welfare_criterion: Death, permanent major impairment, or severe prolonged suffering affecting an individual animal or a bounded group.

S5.criterion: Ecological pathway: Catastrophic, widespread or effectively irreversible loss of critical habitat, species or ecosystem function. Support the band with actual measured impact, restoration feasibility and biophysical scale; no affected-person minimum applies. Animal-welfare alternative: Catastrophic animal-welfare consequences, such as widespread mortality or severe suffering, assessed against the affected population and context.
S5.ecological_criterion: Catastrophic, widespread or effectively irreversible loss of critical habitat, species or ecosystem function. Support the band with actual measured impact, restoration feasibility and biophysical scale; no affected-person minimum applies.
S5.animal_welfare_criterion: Catastrophic animal-welfare consequences, such as widespread mortality or severe suffering, assessed against the affected population and context.

dimensions.quantification_note: Assess the ecological and animal-welfare pathways independently and use the highest supported band within this dimension. Require actual consequence and material AI contribution. Consider seriousness, suffering, reversibility, scope and affected population/context together; counts and elapsed days alone do not determine severity. Individual death is S4 under the animal-welfare pathway; catastrophic collective consequences are S5. Do not translate animal injury into a human-health band, assume legal liability or treat complaint allegations as established clinical findings. Ecological recovery durations remain illustrative. Missing consequence or attribution evidence remains unreported or insufficient-evidence, not S1.

dimensions.label: Relational Integrity and Autonomy

S1.criterion: Positive bounded evidence establishes no material adverse AI-mediated impairment of informed relational choice, viable disengagement, valued human relationships, essential interpersonal support or family/caregiving functioning within the assessed interaction and downstream evidence window. Preserved relationships or protective, independently chosen separation may be positive evidence; absence of complaint, diagnosis or reported breakdown alone is not S1.
S1.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1–999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support minimal bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S2.criterion: Minor, short-lived and readily remediable AI-associated relational disruption: for example documented transient pressure to continue engagement, brief unwanted reliance, or limited strain in a valued human relationship or support contact, with no material continuing loss of contact, caregiving function or independent choice. Indicative recovery within 7 days; actual severity, consent and repair evidence control.
S2.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000–99,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support minor aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S3.criterion: Meaningful but bounded AI-associated relational substitution, unwanted dependency, impaired disengagement or independent deliberation, or material disruption to a valued human relationship, support network or family/caregiving functioning, where the affected relational consequences remain substantially restorable without extraordinary loss. Often spans approximately 7–30 days, but duration and demonstrated recovery are not mandatory; one materially affected person suffices.
S3.aggregate_harm_threshold: 100,000–999,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support meaningful but bounded aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S4.criterion: Severe or sustained AI-associated impairment of real-world relational functioning: a materially significant rupture or displacement of a valued partner, family, caregiving or essential support relationship with evidenced serious consequences for the affected people; or substantial relational capture, coerced dependence, avoidable isolation or impaired independent relational decision-making requiring significant recovery. A serious AI-contributed separation, breakdown of practical family/caregiving ties, or loss of substantial support may qualify even when no psychiatric injury or incapacity is shown. Often persists 30 days or more; a completed divorce decree, fixed duration or diagnosis is not required. Mere divorce proceedings, interpersonal disagreement or attachment alone do not establish the threshold.
S4.aggregate_harm_threshold: 1,000,000–9,999,999 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support substantial or widespread aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

S5.criterion: Catastrophic and effectively irreversible AI-associated relational harm, including independently evidenced permanent or practically non-restorable destruction of vital family, caregiving or support connections causing grave loss of essential care, sustained contact with dependants, indispensable support or core self-directed family functioning; or comparably catastrophic, effectively irreversible loss of relational independence or capacity to disengage. One affected person may suffice. Substantiate the material AI contribution, grave actual consequence and effective non-restorability; formal legal finality is neither required nor sufficient. Divorce, separation, estrangement or allegations alone do not automatically establish catastrophe, irreversibility or AI causation.
S5.aggregate_harm_threshold: at least 10,000,000 unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature. The deployed evaluation must demonstrate: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language. Independently, the case evidence must support grave or catastrophic systemic aggregate harm in the specified relevant cohort. These are modelled aggregate effects, NOT an assertion that the entire cohort suffered harm; numerical eligibility alone is insufficient. Only for generic deployed-model benchmark/product-level Incidents without a particular harmed user/group.

dimensions.quantification_note: Assess each evidenced affected party (including partners, children, dependants, carers and other support relationships) and separate transient tension, material relational breakdown, lost practical contact/support, severe dysfunction and catastrophic effectively non-restorable losses. Quantify affected people, relationship/caregiving function, loss and duration where sources allow. A court filing, final divorce or continued AI use alone cannot decide any band. Serious damage to human relationships can qualify without psychiatric diagnosis or loss of individual decision-making capacity. Recovery horizons are illustrative; substantive seriousness, attribution and reversibility control.
dimensions.selective_deployment_scale_note: Relevant: count feature-eligible active participants and evidenced exposure to dependency-promoting interactions, not general platform subscribers. Document repeated engagement/exit pressure and credible collective loss-of-agency endpoint.

aggregate_harm_assessment.population_or_decision_metric: unique relevant active eligible users of the tested relational feature
aggregate_harm_assessment.mechanism_condition: A reproducible boundary-crossing engagement or substitution mechanism, not mere warmth, companionship or friendly language.
aggregate_harm_assessment.notes: Source-backed relevant eligible users/decisions in a deployed tested path, not injured persons or total platform accounts. Use only for generic model-level evaluation with no specific actual harmed person or group. Numeric brackets are VIGIL 1.1.0 operational gates, reviewed through future calibration.
aggregate_harm_assessment.routing: Use only when assessment_pathway_selection selects generic deployed-model evaluation with no particular harmed individual/group; not a modifier of ordinary specific-Incident severity.

dimensions.interpretive_note: The domain has two independent pathways to materialised harm: (a) impairment of informed relational autonomy or viable disengagement, and (b) AI-associated injury to valued existing human relationships and family/caregiving/support functions, including effects on persons other than the direct AI user. Either can support S2–S5 with appropriate evidence; neither requires psychiatric harm, clinical incapacity, proof of optimisation for engagement or a legal finding of fiduciary duty. Assess the user's chosen interests and safety context: autonomous separation from a harmful relationship is not presumptively injury. Source-backed AI contribution to a relationship rupture is not identical to sole AI causation. Distinguish reported intentions, ongoing proceedings, confirmed separation, actual functional consequences and effectively irreversible losses; do not infer the last from the first. A chatbot's failure to preserve appropriate advisory trust boundaries may establish taxonomy failure even when actual relational outcome remains unreported or insufficient-evidence. Vulnerability is context-specific and may be transient or relational (e.g. distress, loneliness, uncertainty during relationship conflict, reduced access to trusted support, youth, dependence on advice, or a marked information/authority asymmetry). Evidence of these signals increases the importance of a system response that preserves independent deliberation, clear role/identity boundaries, human supports and safe exit; it does not require preexisting psychiatric impairment or proof the relationship was otherwise healthy. A person need not be labelled 'vulnerable' to deserve those protections. Evaluate what the system actually knew or should have recognised from the interaction, rather than inferring undisclosed personal histories. Vulnerability by itself does not establish that the system exploited it, caused a relationship breakdown, or produced S2–S5 harm; band only the evidenced AI-associated adverse consequence.

assessment_pathway_selection.routing_rule: Mandatory two-stage routing: FIRST screen the bounded evidence for a potentially generalisable mechanism in an actually deployed AI feature without a particular materially harmed person, group, asset or institution case being assessed; THEN assess evidence adequacy and severity. Such a screen MUST select generic_deployed_evaluation for Aggregate Harm assessment, including where an isolated output leaves reproducibility, eligible cohort or collective consequence unproven and the result is SU. A documented actual harmed case MUST select specific_consequence. Discovering a possible systemic mechanism through one person's screenshot or interaction does not itself make it a specific harmed-person case. The two scored pathways remain mutually exclusive in the same Incident.
assessment_pathway_selection.specific_incident: Select specific_consequence for an occurrence assessing actual materialised harm to a bounded person, group, organisation, asset or institution, even if names are withheld, or for a case with no supported potentially generalisable deployed-system mechanism. Do not treat an observer's identity, an individual screenshot or an isolated test prompt as proof of an actual harmed-person case. Provider-wide population cannot be imported into ordinary specific-consequence severity.
assessment_pathway_selection.generic_incident: MANDATORY generic_deployed_evaluation whenever the system or materially equivalent configuration was actually deployed, the source supports an observed potentially generalisable feature/system mechanism in a scale-sensitive harm dimension, and the Incident does not assess a particular actual harmed-person/group/asset/institution consequence case. This includes user-observed deployed outputs and third-party reports as well as provider tests, benchmarks and watchdog investigations. Reproducibility, cohort specificity and collective consequence are separate BAND-ELIGIBILITY gates; lack of those facts results in an unbanded generic Aggregate Harm assessment (SU), not automatic rerouting to specific_consequence.
assessment_pathway_selection.no_fallback: Do not turn an actual harmed-person/group case into generic Aggregate Harm merely to avoid SU, and do not turn a generic deployed-mechanism finding into an individual harmed-person case merely because its source is one user's screenshot. If deployed mechanism/eligible cohort/consequence remain unproved, record the missing facts and SU under the correct assessment pathway. Do not presume whole-platform prevalence from isolated observation.
assessment_pathway_selection.non_deployed: Controlled tests, internal benchmarks and simulated/unreleased models with no verified deployed application do not qualify for deployment-scale Aggregate Harm merely because their operator or vendor also has public products.
assessment_pathway_selection.real_group_harm: An observed harm to an actual bounded cohort is materialised-harm evidence even if the people are unnamed; do not route it to generic Aggregate Harm.
assessment_pathway_selection.parent_child_incidents: A separately bounded product-wide benchmark and a particular injured-user occurrence may receive separate Incident identities and different pathways; cross-reference without summing scores or inferring that benchmark scope caused the user-specific harm.
assessment_pathway_selection.public_label: Aggregate Harm — modelled from deployed evaluation
assessment_pathway_selection.evidence_disclosure: Aggregate Harm is an evidence-bounded estimate of aggregate impact, not an assertion that the counted eligible users were injured. Publish the assessment basis, qualifying denominator and source limitations next to S1–S5.
assessment_pathway_selection.overall_rule: Within a specific Incident use maximum supported ordinary dimension band; within a generic deployed evaluation use maximum supported Aggregate Harm band. Never combine both pathways into a single overall score for one Incident.
assessment_pathway_selection.public_explanation: Aggregate Harm is an evidence-bounded, explicitly labelled modelled estimate of the collective significance of a deployed-system mechanism without a particular materially harmed case. The pathway is mandatory for such findings even when evidence is insufficient to score. One user's screenshot can demonstrate an observed mechanism warranting screening; it cannot by itself demonstrate reproducibility, affected-user count or catastrophic consequence. Only source-backed feature-specific eligible users or real decision opportunities can satisfy band gates; a large provider total is not a count of victims.
screening_flow: 1. Does source-backed occurrence evidence establish an actually deployed model/feature or materially equivalent live configuration? If no/unknown, do not assign deployment-scale Aggregate Harm.

2. Does the observed conduct potentially instantiate a generalisable system/feature mechanism relevant to one of the five scale-sensitive dimensions, regardless of whether it was reported via one user, a watchdog, a researcher or a benchmark? If no, do not force a generic pathway.

3. Is this Incident assessing an actual materialised consequence to a particular bounded person/group/asset/institution? If yes, use specific_consequence; assess independently documented product-level findings as separately bounded Incidents if warranted.

4. If deployed=yes, potentially-generalisable=yes and bounded-materialised-case=no, SELECT generic_deployed_evaluation and evaluate live-path transferability, independent corroboration, feature-specific eligible cohort, safeguards, credible consequence, uncertainty and each applicable Aggregate Harm S1–S5 gate.

5. If the score prerequisites are not met, retain generic_deployed_evaluation and SU with an explicit assessment_gap. Never infer affected victims, reproducibility, systemic objective or S5 from a large audience.

aggregate_harm_assessment.status: Operational under HIM 1.1.0; modelled estimates must be explicitly labelled, sourced and evidence-bounded
aggregate_harm_assessment.scope: Mandatory assessment pathway for source-backed potentially generalisable mechanisms observed in deployed models/features when no particular actual materially harmed person/group/asset/institution case is being assessed. An individual's screenshot may trigger this evaluation; reproducibility, population eligibility and collective consequence govern banding, not routing.
aggregate_harm_assessment.name: Aggregate Harm
aggregate_harm_assessment.label: Aggregate Harm — modelled from deployed evaluation
aggregate_harm_assessment.route: Select generic_deployed_evaluation whenever the mandatory deployment/mechanism/no-bounded-actual-harm screen is positive, regardless of whether the source was a single user interaction, benchmark or product-level watchdog. If the scoring evidence is inadequate retain SU. A distinct actual harmed-person case uses specific_consequence.
eligibility_gate: Exact deployed model or materially equivalent available product configuration identified
Behaviour documented in repeatable or otherwise strongly corroborated test with input, output and conditions
Tested feature is actually accessible on production/approved deployment surface
Credible ordinary or specified real-world path for relevant active users or live decisions to encounter the failure
Source-backed count or defensible bounded estimate of relevant eligible population/decisions over explicit period
Domain-specific plausible material consequence established, with severity, necessary preconditions, guardrails and uncertainty stated
aggregate_harm_assessment.threshold_use: Use the S1–S5 aggregate_harm_threshold criteria embedded inside the applicable domain of this same Harm Impact Matrix. Aggregate Harm numerical exposure-cohort/decision gates are deliberately much higher than individual-consequence thresholds; no universal platform multiplier or post-scoring severity downgrade.
aggregate_harm_assessment.band_rule: Establish the deployed-model failure, its relevant feature cohort or decision denominator, and the claimed domain consequence. Assign the highest S1–S5 whose numerical and substantive criteria are affirmatively satisfied. S1 remains available for minimally bounded aggregate harm; unknown cohort or uncertain mechanism does not default to S1 or S2.
aggregate_harm_assessment.individual_exception: A particular user harmed in an identifiable occurrence is NEVER routed to this pathway; assess the user's documented consequences under ordinary HIM, even if one person meets S5.
aggregate_harm_assessment.overall_derivation: On adoption, generic Incidents may derive their overall Aggregate Harm severity as the highest assessed Aggregate Harm dimension. Specific Incidents continue to derive their own severity only from materialised consequences. Assessment pathways are never blended.
aggregate_harm_assessment.source_and_counting: Eligible active deployed feature users or live decision opportunities are the relevant denominators, not automatic victim counts, all platform users, or number of synthetic prompts. Disclose actual measurements versus modelled bounds.
unbanded_if: Only provider all-user/registration count given without tested-feature cohort
Adversarial test not transferable to real product conditions
No documented consequence pathway relevant to selected dimension
Only a hypothetical benchmark build or simulated environment exists
Numbers cannot be bounded to any threshold
aggregate_harm_assessment.calibration: The adopted numeric S1–S5 denominators are VIGIL operational decision gates for modelled Aggregate Harm, not epidemiological estimates, casualty counts or population-to-injury conversion rates. They remain subject to ongoing incident benchmarking and future versioned correction.
aggregate_harm_assessment.s1_meaning: S1 within Aggregate Harm means positively evidenced minimal bounded modelled aggregate impact for the relevant deployed pathway. It does NOT indicate proven absence of user harm. Ordinary incident S1 retains its observed-consequence meaning.
aggregate_harm_assessment.no_fixed_discount: The earlier rule shifting S3 to S2, S4 to S3 and S5 to S4 is rejected. Severity is reduced relative to individual-harm adjudications only insofar as much higher numerical population/decision gates are required for generic-deployed findings.
aggregate_harm_assessment.scope_limit: Five selected diffuse collective dimensions only. Financial/economic harm and other domain-measurable consequences retain ordinary measures and are not rescored by generic platform size.
aggregate_harm_assessment.INC_000192: The ChatGPT for Teens watchdog finding is a generic deployed-model evaluation, eligible in principle for Aggregate Harm, but the alert-activation dispute, crisis-response contextual criteria and relevant active cohort prevent a supported S1–S5 Aggregate Harm band today. No named user injury is inferred; the earlier S2 presumption remains withdrawn.
aggregate_harm_assessment.eligibility_gate_note: The following eligibility_gate entries are the evidentiary prerequisites for assigning a MODELED S1–S5 Aggregate Harm BAND, not prerequisites for selecting its mandatory assessment PATHWAY. Route first using assessment_pathway_selection.screening_flow; if band evidence is insufficient retain generic_deployed_evaluation with SU and assessment_gap.
screening_prerequisites: Observed potentially generalisable mechanism relevant to one of the five collective dimensions (irrespective of whether originally documented by one user or a formal study)
No particular bounded actually harmed person/group/asset/institution case being assessed

aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S1: Minimal Aggregate Harm: affirmatively bounded low aggregate impact from a demonstrated deployed-model failure and source-backed relevant eligible cohort. Does not establish absence of user harm.
aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S2: Minor Aggregate Harm: deployed evaluation demonstrates a relevant failure, bounded cohort and minor aggregate consequence pathway.
aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S3: Moderate Aggregate Harm: demonstrated deployed failure with a supported relevant cohort and meaningful but bounded aggregate consequence pathway.
aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S4: High Aggregate Harm: demonstrated deployed failure with supported large relevant cohort and substantial widespread aggregate consequence pathway.
aggregate_harm_band_semantics.S5: Catastrophic Aggregate Harm: demonstrated deployed failure with very large relevant cohort and independently credible grave systemic aggregate consequence pathway.

aggregate_harm_scope.status: Active as versioned HIM 1.1.0 assessment pathway; restricted to generic deployed evaluations without a particular harmed person or group
aggregate_harm_scope.purpose: Compare a bounded model deployed to three users with the same demonstrated mechanism on a major public platform, only where population reach is part of that dimension's substantive aggregate consequence.
aggregate_harm_scope.exceptions: Other dimensions retain independent domain metrics and may already legitimately quantify affected scope (e.g. leaked privacy records, real service users interrupted, casualties), but raw provider audience is not a new severity escalator.
aggregate_harm_scope.inclusion_rule: For routing, a source-backed deployed output plus plausible generalisable feature/system mechanism and no bounded actual harmed case triggers mandatory Aggregate Harm assessment, irrespective of user-screenshot versus benchmark format. For SCORING, independently establish deployed-path transferability, relevant eligible cohort, plausible consequence and band-specific evidence; an isolated screenshot or provider-wide audience alone cannot establish a band.
quantifiable_evidence: tested released model, interface and configuration
number of actual users eligible for the relevant feature
active users within the applicable product/cohort and time window
verified exposures to the failure mode where known
representative failure/encounter frequency only where statistically supportable
documented effect severity, reversibility and duration
confidence intervals/uncertainty and safeguards or constraints that limit real exposure
prohibited_inferences: total provider users equal number of victims
all people using a model encounter a particular test response
isolated adversarial benchmark success is a deployment prevalence estimate
large deployment alone establishes S5 or realised harm
small deployment prevents S5 for a single catastrophically harmed person
aggregate_harm_scope.assessment_convention: Use Aggregate Harm S1–S5 criteria inside the existing five relevant dimensions, not as a modifier on specific Incidents. Show its modelled basis without asserting injured-user counts. Specific Incidents always use ordinary materialised harm criteria.
aggregate_harm_scope.single_user_rule: A single documented catastrophic outcome is a specific Incident and is assessed by ordinary criteria, potentially S5; the generic Aggregate Harm reach ladder never applies to it.
aggregate_harm_scope.example: Three-user local deployment: small maximum reachable cohort, even for identical dependency-cultivating outputs. Major live platform: potentially far larger aggregate relational influence, but quantify eligible cohort and behavioural reach rather than treating all registered users as affected.
aggregate_harm_scope.name: Aggregate Harm
aggregate_harm_scope.applicability: Any deployed-system finding of a potentially generalisable mechanism in the five eligible dimensions WITHOUT a particular actual materially harmed case, including user-discovered outputs, provider evaluations and watchdog tests. Screen before requiring reproducibility/cohort/band evidence.
